A country just deployed 27,500 GPUs for national AI.

Japan and NVIDIA announced a partnership to build the world's first national AI infrastructure for physical AI. Not research. Not policy. Real compute at industrial scale — 13,750 Vera CPUs and 27,500 Rubin GPUs deployed through Noetra, targeting manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and telecom.

The phrase 'physical AI' carries enormous weight here. This is not about chatbots or content generation. Japan is building sovereign infrastructure for robotics, automation, and AI systems that operate in the real world.

For business leaders, this creates a new strategic dimension. Countries investing in dedicated AI infrastructure become magnets for enterprise deployment. They offer compute access, regulatory clarity, and workforce ecosystems that reduce friction at every layer.

Japan is not alone. South Korea committed $880 billion over ten years to semiconductors and AI. The competitive landscape is shifting from company versus company to nation versus nation.

The executives who understand this shift will choose where to build based on infrastructure strategy, not just labor costs.
